subject: Cross-region DR responsibilities and proposed SLA addendum
messages:
From: Jake Morris <jake.morris@atlaspay.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlaspay.com>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-region failover responsibilities and RTO/RPO expectations

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — AtlasPay is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move forward with a PO, procurement needs clarity on how Redwood handles multi-region failover and what exceptions (if any) you can make to the standard SLA for our use case. A few specifics from our side: 

- We have strict data-residency constraints in us-east-1 that prevent full replication of certain PII stores to eu-west-1.
- For payments reconciliation, we need a guaranteed recovery time objective and an acceptable data-loss window during a regional outage.
- We are evaluating two options: 1) Redwood provides a formal SLA addendum for cross-region failover with explicit RTO/RPO, or 2) we take dedicated/reserved capacity with a simpler SLA.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept an SLA addendum that:
- Defines an RTO of 4 hours for service rehydration in a secondary region, and
- Accepts an RPO up to 1 hour for user state (non-transactional PII handled separately),
- Includes expectations around degraded throughput during failover (e.g. 50% baseline throughput until warm caches rebuild).

I attached a short summary of AtlasPay's DR constraints (atlaspay_dr_requirements.pdf). Our procurement/legal team would like a draft addendum and an initial timeline for signing.

Appreciate a quick confirm that this is on the table — if not, please advise the minimum changes Redwood can accept and the cost delta for dedicated capacity.

Regards,
Jake Morris
Head of Infrastructure, AtlasPay
Phone: +1 415 555 0133

Attachment: atlaspay_dr_requirements.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jake Morris <jake.morris@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-region failover responsibilities and proposed SLA addendum

Hi Jake — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. I'm looping in Markus (Infrastructure SLA lead) and Lauren (Legal/program ops) to align on a path forward. Short answer: we can offer a scoped SLA addendum for cross-region failover, but it will need to be explicit about scope, capacity guarantees, and the operational triggers for failover. 

High-level proposal (internal summary):
- Interim DR coverage (addendum):
  • RTO target: <= 4 hours from failover trigger to service acceptance in secondary region (best-effort if not on dedicated capacity).
  • RPO target: <= 1 hour for application state we manage (we will exclude certain PII datasets as noted).
  • Throughput expectation during failover: baseline throughput may degrade to 40–60% until caches and autoscaling converge.
- Hard guarantees (SLA-backed) require Reserved/Dedicated capacity with explicit node counts — we can provide a sizing worksheet and cost delta.

Next steps: I will share a draft addendum (attached) with explicit trigger language and an operational runbook excerpt. Could we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the AtlasPay team through the trade-offs?

I attached: proposed_sla_addendum_v2.pdf and redwood_sla_matrix.csv (contains capacity vs. latency estimates).

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_sla_addendum_v2.pdf, redwood_sla_matrix.csv

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-region failover responsibilities and proposed SLA addendum (internal)

Quick internal take after a first pass on AtlasPay's ask: 

- Risk: granting a firm RTO/RPO across regions for multi-tenant pools without dedicated capacity materially increases blast radius. During a primary-region outage we may be forced to rehydrate large KV caches that will cause sustained CPU/GPU pressure and could increase latency for co-tenants.
- Recommendation: push for Reserved/Dedicated nodes as the default for SLA-backed cross-region failover. If they insist on an addendum for multi-tenant pools, make it limited:
  1) Exception window: SLA applies only for the first 90 days post-PO while we validate runbook; revert to best-effort thereafter unless Reserved capacity purchased.
  2) Include clear fallback: automatic failback, and a throughput floor (e.g., 40%) to protect other customers.
  3) Require a red-team DR run prior to any SLA enforcement and quarterly DR tests.

I'll draft suggested language for section 3 (operational triggers + limits) and send by EOD. Legal will need to approve the exception language.

-Markus
Director, Infrastructure & SLAs

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jake Morris <jake.morris@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlaspay.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-region failover responsibilities and proposed SLA addendum

Jake — looping Priya so procurement has visibility; Markus and Lauren added language per our internal review.

On Tue, May 1, 2028 at 9:15 AM Jake Morris <jake.morris@atlaspay.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept an SLA addendum that:
> - Defines an RTO of 4 hours for service rehydration in a secondary region, and
> - Accepts an RPO up to 1 hour for user state...

Attached is a revised draft (proposed_sla_addendum_v2.pdf). Key changes since my note:
- Explicit trigger definition: primary-region declared outage must be confirmed by both AtlasPay and Redwood on-call before SLA countdown begins.
- Two-tier model:
  * Tier A (Reserved capacity): SLA-backed RTO <= 4h / RPO <= 1h / throughput floor = 90% of baseline.
  * Tier B (Multi-tenant, exception addendum): best-effort RTO <= 4h with documented caveats, RPO <= 1h best-effort, throughput floor = 40–60%. Exception is timeboxed and subject to quarterly DR validation.
- Obligations: AtlasPay must provide a runbook and a list of critical keys that need prioritized warming; Redwood will provide a warm-cache priority API as an operational control.

Can you confirm whether Tier B (exception addendum) is acceptable to procurement/legal while we size Reserved capacity for Tier A? If yes, we'll circulate for signature and include a single DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Camila

Attachment: proposed_sla_addendum_v2.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jake Morris <jake.morris@atlaspay.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 May 2028 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-region failover responsibilities and proposed SLA addendum — DocuSign and next steps

Hi Jake / Priya — thanks for the quick review and the call earlier this week. Per your feedback, legal approved the exception language for Tier B with the following commitments:

- Redwood will issue the addendum for Tier B as drafted (timeboxed exception, quarterly DR validation, throughput floor 40–60%).
- If AtlasPay upgrades to Reserved capacity within 90 days we will convert to Tier A terms retroactively from the upgrade date.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.example.com/doc/ATLAS-5692
Estimated timeline: procurement signature within 3–7 business days -> counter-signed by Redwood within 2 business days -> kickoff for DR run with Infrastructure (Markus) scheduled within 10 business days after final signature.

I've created JIRA RED-2314 to track the DR run and legal checklist. I've attached the final addendum and the capacity sizing spreadsheet. Let me know if you want the Reserved capacity pricing broken out by node type — happy to send a one-pager.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_sla_addendum_v2.pdf, redwood_sla_matrix.csv
